findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple areas in the physical facility needing repair:
1) SECOND REPEAT: Under the left side of the sink at the dish machine there are multiple tiles that have come loose from the wall.
2) SECOND REPEAT: The bar hand-sink needs sealed to the wall. Facilities that cannot be moved for cleaning should be adhered to the wall to prevent the entry and harborage of mold.
3) FIRST REPEAT There are tiles underneath the dry storage along the north wall of the kitchen have separated from the wall.
Ensure repairs are made by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed shrimp being thawed in the basin of the hand washing sink next to the kitchen office. CORRECTED- shrimp was removed from the sink. Ensure hand washing sinks are used for no other purpose than hand washing, so as to not deter hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple areas in the facility needing repair:
1) FIRST REPEAT: Under the left side of the sink at the dish machine there are multiple tiles that have come loose from the wall.
2) FIRST REPEAT: The bar hand-sink needs caulked to the wall. Facilities that cannot be moved for cleaning should be adhered to the wall to be made smooth and easily cleanable.

Ensure repairs are made by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT: None of the facility’s Certified Food Protection Managers (CFPM)s have allergen awareness certificates. Allergen Awareness information (given during the previous inspection) is in black binder with the other paperwork. Certified Food Protection Managers are required to obtain allergen awareness training in Class I facilities. Certificates must be renewed every 3 years.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.[C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the basin of the  handwashing sink at the facility’s bar to be obstructed by a container of Clorox wipes. CORRECTED- the wipes were removed. Ensure handwashing sinks are made available for handwashing only at all times.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.[Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Multiple food contact surfaces were found to contain an accumulation of soil debris:
1) Back of the ice baffles in the large server prep room.
2) Soda nozzles of the bar server station.
CORRECTED- the ice machine was emptied and wiped with a clean sanitizer rag. The soda nozzles were removed to be cleaned, brushed, and sanitized.
Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of soil debris. This frequency may need to increase with use and variable outdoor temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
None of the facility’s CFMs have allergen awareness certificates. Discussion was had between inspector and PIC, and inspector gave the PIC a list of accredited institutes for allergen awareness training. Certified Food Protection Managers are required to obtain allergen awareness training. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.[C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: The manager’s Certified Food Protection Manager’s certificate recently expired and they have not retaken the test yet. Ensure that there is always a CFPM on site during all hours of operation. The PIC stated that he will be taking it soon and did not realize that it had expired.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: There was raw meat observed to be stored above potatoes and rolls in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- The raw meat was moved from above these items and staff was educated on storage order. Ensure that food is protected from cross contamination during storage and holding. 

 (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P).

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
5-205.15: There was a leak observed in the triple sink faucet. Ensure that this leak is repaired by next routine inspection. Plumbing systems should be maintained in good repair. 

A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Conveyor belt dish machine final rinse observed reaching less than 160F, according to the a heat-sensing sticker and inspector’s plate thermometer. PIC restarted the booster, at which time the machine reached at least 160F on the heat sensing sticker and 180F on the machine’s built-in baffle thermometer.
4-501.112: (A) Temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse may not be more than 194F or less than 160F for stationary rack, single temperature machines. All other machines can be no less than 180F. (B) Maximum temperature does not apply to high pressure and temperature systems with wand-type spraying devices. [P]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: No ambient thermometer is present in the 2 door cooler near the back door. CORRECTED- A thermometer was moved from the out-of-use salad bowl cooler. Ensure thermometers are present in all cold holding equipment. (Previously observed 10/25/2023.)
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. [C]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
There is a gap along the bottom of the windowed back door where daylight is visible when the door is shut. Add a sweep or otherwise close the gap so that the door is tight-fitting and protected against pests.
6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent. [C]

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
Facility does not have a vomit/diarrhea clean up policy on file. CORRECTED- Inspector emailed a clean up policy to be printed and kept on site in case norovirus disinfection is needed.
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Sanitizer bucket near the salad prep area observed with 100 ppm quat sanitizer. CORRECTED- PIC remade sanitizer bucket to 200ppm quat.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have a concentration based on the label (200-400ppm). [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
-Heavy cream observed in the bar cooler without any date-marking. CORRECTED- Un-dated heavy cream was voluntarily discarded.
-Orange juice in the bar cooler observed with a written date mark of 10/20, and a manufacturer use by date of 10/19. CORRECTED- Orange juice was voluntarily discarded.
-BP glaze in the walk-in cooler observed with a date marking of 10/15. CORRECTED- Glaze was voluntarily discarded.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1. (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date. (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food. (D) Approved date marking systems. (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container. (F) Does not apply to shellstock.  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma). [Pf]

findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Mold was observed on the baffle in the ice machine bin. Kitchen manager noted inside the ice machine bin was just cleaned about 2 weeks ago. Ensure cleaning occurs as needed to eliminate buildup.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18 (A) Heavy whipping cream in the bar cooler had a date mark of 9/8 and was past the seven day time frame for use. Whipping cream was discarded. Ensure date marked foods are used or discarded within seven days. Discard products at the close of business on the 7th day to ensure compliance. 
A food specified in  3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in  3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in  3501.17(A).

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12 1. Scoop used for whole coffee beans was on top of the coffee maker where some dust accumulation was observed. Scoop was removed for cleaning and storage in a clean container was discussed.
2. Ice scoop holder at south server area was observed with a small piece of debris in the bottom. Holder and scoop were removed for cleaning. 
3. Ice scoop holders attached to soda machine at the bar and the ice bin in the bar had some dust accumulation on inner surfaces. Ensure cleaning of holders as needed to eliminate accumulation of dust. 
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils shall be stored in clean, protected location if utensils, such as ice scoops, are used only with non-TCS food.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(1) Some foods in the steam table were observed with internal temperatures below 135F and included mashed potatoes (117F), a portion of lasagna (97F-119F), and red sauce (124F). Other foods were observed with internal temperatures at 140F/above depending on when product was prepared and placed in the holding wells. Mashed potatoes were replaced with fresh product, which was observed with an internal temperature of 164F in the warmer. Lasagna was discarded as another portion of lasagna with an internal temperature of 143F was available for service. Red sauces were reheated to 165F prior to placing back in the steam table for service.
Water in the main holding well was observed at 170F, but products in the steam table were double panned. Double panning is not best practice if hot water is not adequate in the second pan to help maintain foods at 135F/above during hot holding. Kitchen manager stated he would change his process for hot holding at the steam table and monitor temperatures to verify best practice for hot holding.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 (B) Open carton of whipping cream in the bar cooler was not date marked. Product was opened over the weekend on Saturday. Whipping cream was dated and kept for use. Whipping cream was also observed without a proper date mark at the bar during the previous routine inspection. Ensure proper date marks for all prepared TCS foods.
Refrigerated, ready to eat TCS food prepared and packaged by a food processing plant shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in ¶ (A). The day the original container is opened in the food establishment shall be counted as Day 1, and the day or date marked by the food establishment may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:

Ensure all staff that are not certified food managers complete an online food handler certification course within 30 days of hiring, and maintain copies of certifications on-site.
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Kitchen manager is currently the only person with a food manager certification and has not completed the food allergen awareness certification. Other members of the staff have the allergen certification but are not currently certified food managers. Management was advised as to the need for the certified food manager to complete the allergen course. Ensure the kitchen manager completes the food allergen certification by the next routine inspection.
Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solution in cook line sani-bucket was observed at a concentration below 100ppm. Solution was prepared recently, and it appeared one of the tablets may have stuck to and possible dissolved into a wiping cloth. Additional tablets were added and brought the concentration to 200ppm
Sanitizer tablets were not dissolving in the server area sani-bucket due to the use of cold water to make the solution. Kitchen manager remade the solution with warm water, and the concentration was observed at 200ppm. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(1) Meat sauce and marinara in the warmer had internal temperatures of 121F and 111F. Kitchen manager noted the warmer was turned on around the same time the products were placed inside after being made fresh this afternoon. Alfredo sauce in the warmer had an internal temperate of 144F. All products in the warmer below 135F were reheated to 165F/above prior to placing back in the warmer for hot holding. Ensure hot holding equipment is on and at proper temperature to maintain hot foods at 135F/above prior to hot holding.  
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18 (A) 1. Spinach dip and scampi butter in the walk-in cooler had prep dates of 12/20 and 12/16. Foods were discarded during inspection.
2. Open carton of whipping cream in the bar cooler was not date marked. Product was likely opened the evening prior. Whipping cream was dated and kept for use.
A food specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in ¶ 3501.17(A).

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 Thawed portions of vacuum packaged fish were observed in the kitchen reach-in cooler. Proper thawing of ROP fish was discussed. Packaging for thawed portions of fish was cut open during inspection. Ensure moving forward that packaging is cut prior to beginning thawing process for ROP fish. 
Reduced oxygen packaged fish that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in ¶(A) of this section; or prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in ¶ (B) of this section.
